did_you_know.text: Did you know? Proverbs 17 presents a dry crust eaten in peace as better than a wealthy house filled with feasting but also with strife, emphasizing that peace is more valuable than wealth without tranquility.
Did you know? This verse compares the testing of the heart to the testing of silver and gold in a furnace: just as metal is tested through refining, so the Lord examines the human heart.
Did you know? According to this verse, anyone who mocks the poor insults not only the person but also his Maker; and anyone who rejoices at another’s misfortune will not go unpunished.
Did you know? This verse connects covering an offense with pursuing love, and warns that repeatedly bringing up the same matter can separate close friends.

Did you know? The beginning of a quarrel is compared to opening a dam: just as released water spreads, a conflict can quickly get out of control. It is therefore better to walk away before the quarrel erupts.
Did you know? The chapter defines a true friend as someone who loves at all times, and adds that a brother is born to stand by you in times of trouble.

Did you know? This verse asks what good it does for a fool to have money to buy wisdom when he lacks the heart for it—meaning that outward resources are not enough without an inner willingness to understand.

Did you know? Proverbs describes a joyful heart as beneficial to the body, while a broken spirit dries up the bones. This is a poetic description of the connection between one’s emotional state and sense of vitality.
Did you know? This verse warns that a bribe accepted in secret can pervert the course of justice, presenting corruption as a direct violation of fair judgment.

Did you know? The chapter praises the person who uses few words and the one who remains calm, and the next verse adds that even a fool may be considered wise if he keeps silent and does not reveal his foolishness.
